newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell names Douglas Aircraft head.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell names Douglas Aircraft head.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said Friday it named Walter Orlowski as president of Douglas Aircraft Co, its commercial aircraft unit in Long Beach, Calif., effective February 1.
Orlowski, 53, had been vice president-general manager of the unit.

He suceeds Michael Sears, who was named president of McDonnell Douglas Aerospace, the company's tactical aircraft, missiles and space businesses. Sears, 49, will assume the new post effective February 1.
The aircraft and aerospace company said it also named E. David Spong as vice president and general manager of its C-17 transport program in Long Beach.

Spong, 58, will report to senior vice president Don Kozlowski, who will remain as head of the company's Military Transport Aircraft unit there, it added. Kozlowski, 59, has said he plans to retire later this year.

Orlowski becomes head of Douglas Aircraft after 29 years with the company. Previous posts included vice president of marketing and senior vice president of the MD-11, MD-90 and MD-80 commercial aircraft programs.
He also led the effort that reviewed and then declined to develop a new widebody airliner, the MD-XX.
McDonnell Douglas said Orlowski also was responsible for implementing a strategic collaboration with Boeing Co.

"Walt Orlowski has been preparing throughout his distinguished career for this assignment," Harry Stonecipher, McDonnell Douglas president, said in a statement. "He has worked in product development, engineering, research and development, marketing and program management."
Sears becomes head of the military unit after 27 years at McDonnell Douglas.

Sears, who had assignments in engineering, product development and program management, headed the development of the U.S. Navy's newest strike fighter, the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet, the company said. He also led the development of the navigation and targeting system for the U.S. Air Force F-15.
"Mike Sears will bring the leadership, technological knowledge and customer focus that we need to build on our success in our tactical aircraft, space and missiles business," Stonecipher said.
Stonecipher had served as acting president of the military business since late October of last year. At that time, Herbert Lanese, who had been head of the aerospace business, resigned.
Spong has spent 33 years with the company, and previously was vice president-general manager for integrated product definition and C-17 deputy program manager, McDonnell Douglas said.
